day2_night_phone_1.text: *The old school group chat. 'Read by 3'. Nobody replied. Two days now.*

day2_night_phone_2.text:
*I sent Minsu a message.*

Hey, Minsu. I transferred and you haven't even contacted me.

day2_night_phone_3.text: *10 minutes later. The '...' indicator appeared. Minsu is typing.*

day2_night_phone_4.text: *5 seconds. The typing indicator keeps blinking. Is he writing a long message?*

day2_night_phone_6.text: Yeah doing well. How's it there?

day2_night_phone_7.text: *Usually, an emoticon would follow the question mark. This time, there’s nothing.*

day2_night_phone_8.text: *For a typing indicator that lingered over five seconds, the reply is barely one short line.*

day2_night_phone_9.text:
*I replied.*

Why so formal? Did something happen?

day2_night_phone_10.text: *1 minute. 2 minutes. The typing indicator appears again.*

day2_night_phone_11.text: No. Nothing happened. I was busy.

day2_night_phone_12.text: *Again, none of Minsu’s usual swearing or emojis. All three sentences end with periods.*

day2_night_phone_13.text: *My thumb stayed frozen over the input box for a long time.*
choices: Check the old group chat again
Put the phone down and think

day2_night_ft_messenger.text:
*I sent a reply.*

Hey Minsu, is that really you? This isn't like you. Did something happen?

day2_night_ft_messenger_2.text: *Typing indicator. Blinking forever. Five seconds, ten, twenty.*

day2_night_ft_messenger_3.text: It's me. I'm just a little sleepy.

day2_night_ft_messenger_4.text: *The typing indicator that blinked for 20 seconds disappears, leaving just one short message bubble.*

day2_night_ft_messenger_5.text: *I erased the half-written letters in the input box. When I turned the screen off, only my face remained in the black glass.*

day2_night_sea_1.text: I finished organizing the student council room today.

day2_night_sea_4.text:
*I reply*

See you tomorrow. Good luck getting ready.

day2_night_sea_5.text: Prepare? You're supposed to help me.

day2_night_sea_6.text: I'll be waiting again tomorrow morning

day2_night_sea_7.text: You don't have to come early. It's cold.

day2_night_sea_8.text: I'm not cold. The wind doesn't blow much near the school gate.

day2_night_sea_9_alt.text: Then I'll see you at school tomorrow. Don't stay up too late.

day2_night_sea_9.text: But Saturday is still on, right?

day2_night_sea_14.text: *I set my phone down. Outside the window, the moon hangs in the sky. A chime rang out—different from my usual messenger alert.*

day2_night_sea_14a.text: *A message came through the Student Safety App.*

day2_night_eunsu_1.text: {name}, you did well on your presentation today. You're adapting fast.

day2_night_eunsu_2.text: Can you stop by the teachers' office tomorrow? There's a document I need to check.

day2_night_eunsu_5.text: *The profile photo slot in the student safety app was blank. Beneath the sender's name, instead of a phone number, there was only a gray label reading 'Homeroom Teacher'.*

day2_night_flash_1.text: *I lie under the covers and close my eyes.*

day2_night_flash_2.text: *A rain-soaked school hallway flashes before my eyes. Someone and I are running side by side in drenched uniforms—*

day2_night_flash_3.text: *Holding hands. A girl's hand. A cold hand.*

day2_night_flash_4.text: *"This way" -- someone's voice. A familiar voice.*

day2_night_flash_5.text: *I open my eyes. There's sweat on my forehead.*

day2_night_flash_6.text: *The room is quiet. But the soles of my feet still held the cold of the wet hallway floor.*

day2_night_flash_7.text: *My hand has risen to grip my own shoulder without me realizing—the cool touch from Ms. Eunsu earlier blurring into the cold hand from the flash.*

day2_night_flash_8.text: *I can see the transfer papers under the desk lamp. The corner of the page is folded at the same angle as it was this morning.*

day2_night_search_1.text: *I kick off the blanket and sit up. Sleep won't come. I pick up my phone and type 'Haedoji School' into the search bar.*

day2_night_search_2.text: *The school's official homepage has a principal greeting and timeline. 'Graduation Album' reads 'Coming soon,' and staff listings—including homeroom teacher Park Eunsu—appear without a single photo.*

day2_night_search_3.text: *News search: 'Haedoji School.' No results. The local news tab is empty too. Only 'No documents match your search terms' remains in the center of the screen.*

day2_night_search_4.text: *Nothing but empty gray boxes fills every thumbnail slot.*

day2_night_search_5.text: *The screen brightness lowered on its own. The school's name is still in the search bar. I set the phone down without deleting it.*

day2_night_dream_1.text: *I close my eyes again. This time, I fall asleep.*

day2_night_dream_3.text: *A classroom. But not the current one. The desk arrangement is different. There's a date written on the blackboard but I can't read it.*

day2_night_dream_4.text: *Someone is sitting in the front seat. Long hair. I can only see their back.*

day2_night_dream_6.text: *That person turns around. It's Seolhwa. In the dream, Seolhwa's eyes are dry. The corners of her mouth are raised.*

day2_night_dream_7.text: *Seolhwa opens her mouth, but no sound comes out. Her lips freeze on 'Help—'*

day2_night_dream_7a.text: *Before the rest of the sentence lands, the date on the chalkboard blurs and runs.*

day2_night_dream_8.text: *The classroom grows dark. Seolhwa's face blurs.*

day2_night_wake_1.text: *Just before dawn, my eyes flutter open from shallow sleep. Bluish morning light seeps through a gap in the curtains.*

day2_night_wake_2.text: *Only Seolhwa's smiling face from the dream lingers before my eyes. All sound has faded, yet the shape of her lips remains vivid.*

day2_night_wake_3.text: *Brushing my charging phone beside the pillow, the timetable tab I opened before bed gleams faintly beneath the lock screen.*

day2_night_ft_groupchat.text: *I opened the old group chat. The read count beside the last message had not changed.*

day2_night_ft_groupchat_2.text: *I returned to the chat list and tapped Minsu’s name.*

day2_night_ft_putdown.text: *I laid the phone face down and thought again about the three sentences Minsu had sent.*

day2_night_ft_putdown_2.text: *The phone vibrated on the desk. I turned it face up again.*

day2_night_drawer_1.text: *Restless and still awake, I yank open a dresser drawer to tidy up, only for it to snag halfway on bunched fabric jammed in the track.*

day2_night_drawer_2.text: *When I reached in and pulled it out, it was a folded dress shirt and the buttons were the same color as the ones I wore today.*

day2_night_drawer_3.text: *I turned my collar over. Only two strands of cut thread remained where the trademark should have been.*

day2_night_drawer_4.text: *Had the dry cleaner cut it while removing the name tag? Even my memory of taking the shirt there was hazy.*

day2_night_drawer_5.text: *When I pressed a stiffened pocket with my finger, a dry scrap of paper crumbled inside.*

day2_night_drawer_6.text: *When I laid out the shirt on the drawer and turned the pocket lining inside out, I found scraps of washed paper stuck to the seams.*

day2_night_drawer_7.text: *One corner fell off while I was taking it off. The remaining part had ink spread like a blue stain.*

day2_night_drawer_8.text: *Only strokes like a '7' and the top half of the character 'ok' remain visible.*

day2_night_drawer_9.text: *Maybe the paper had gotten mixed in during the move. I pulled the desk lamp closer over the desk.*

day2_night_drawer_choice.text: *The wet and dry paper was thinly attached to the tip of my fingernail.*
choices: I look at it in the light of the stand
I think I got someone else's laundry mixed up.
Throw the paper in the trash can

day2_night_drawer_light_1.text: *I held the paper close to the lamp. Light leaked from the thinner area, making the black line look different in thickness.*

day2_night_drawer_light_2.text: *Two dots remained next to the 7. Someone may have written down the page number.*

day2_night_drawer_light_3.text: *Even the strokes that looked like 'ok' turn unfamiliar the moment I block part of them.*

day2_night_drawer_light_4.text: *Snapping a photo and zooming in brings up the rough grain of the paper clearer than the ink.*

day2_night_drawer_light_5.text: *I added the date to the photo and slipped the scrap into the notebook's back pocket.*

day2_night_drawer_light_6.text: *I picked up a small piece that had rolled under the desk and put the two sides together, but one stroke was empty.*

day2_night_drawer_light_7.text: *I hung my shirt on a hanger and opened my left sleeve. There was a line on the inside of my wrist that looked like it had been drawn with a pencil.*

day2_night_drawer_light_8.text: *I thought I might have rinsed out less detergent, so I wet my fingertips and rubbed them, but the stain was still there.*

day2_night_drawer_light_9.text: *I decided to look again in the morning light and put my phone down.*

day2_night_drawer_laundry_1.text: *Spreading the shirt over the one I wore today, the shoulders match—only the sleeves come up a knuckle shorter.*

day2_night_drawer_laundry_2.text: *The moving boxes must have gotten mixed up.*

day2_night_drawer_laundry_3.text: *I set the paper scraps aside in an empty envelope. Once I find a dry cleaner in the neighborhood, I should ask about it.*

day2_night_drawer_laundry_4.text: *I write 'Shirt' across the bag, then reach for my phone to check today's date.*

day2_night_drawer_laundry_5.text: *I checked the date printed beneath the class schedule and copied it down. This late at night, I keep double-checking even the simplest things.*

day2_night_drawer_laundry_6.text: *Tomorrow, I should ask where the dry cleaner is first. I folded the shirt and put it on top of the wardrobe.*

day2_night_drawer_bin_1.text: *I threw the paper into the trash can. The flakes on my fingers were wiped off with a wet towel.*

day2_night_drawer_bin_2.text: *A number-like stroke was briefly visible on the bottom of the trash can, but was immediately hidden when a new tissue was placed over it.*

day2_night_drawer_bin_3.text: *The clothes were in good condition, so it was a waste to throw them away. I folded only the cut part of the label inward and hung it on a hanger.*

day2_night_drawer_bin_4.text: *I gathered up the spare uniform button rolling around in the corner of the drawer and tucked it into the same compartment.*

day2_night_drawer_join_1.text: *I had to clear away the things spread out in front of the drawer before I could lie back down in bed.*
choices: Slip the papers into the notebook first
Hang the shirt on a hanger first
Leave the light on while tidying up

day2_night_drawer_join_2.text: *Clicking off the desk lamp leaves only faint window light in the room. I pull the curtains shut a bit tighter.*

day2_night_drawer_join_3.text: *Only after checking twice that the alarm was on did I plug in the charging cable.*

day2_night_drawer_join_4.text: *I tucked the end of the blanket under my feet and lay on my side.*

day2_history_callback_8.text: *I remembered the pen grip I had held in the morning. I also turned the shirt sleeves over from the left, but accidentally changed the order.*

day2_history_callback_9.text: *I remembered Sea's late-night greeting notification from yesterday. Afraid the screen might light up in the middle of the night again, I switched my phone to silent.*

day2_expansion_action_3_a.text: *I wrapped a rubber band around the note to prevent it from opening, checked that the end of the paper was not sticking out, and then pushed the drawer.*

day2_expansion_action_3_b.text: *I adjusted the shoulder line of the shirt and turned the hanger. I was a little less concerned when I couldn't see the cut off brand part.*
